prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Master Your Desktop Pet Controls", "Complete these quick steps to get familiar with managing your desktop companion.", "Try pet movement and desktop visibility controls"]
1: ["Preparing Desktop Engine..."]
2: ["Upload clear photo", "Validation Preview"]
3: ["Choose Your Pet Creation Path", "Select a ready-to-play starter pet or create a unique custom companion from photos."]
4: ["Sign in with your main account to keep your pet save data synced and prevent account resets."]
5: ["Choose Your Companion & Personality", "Select Trait"]
6: ["Bringing Your Pet to Life", "Generating assets and preparing desktop window integration..."]
7: ["Your Pet is Live on Your Desktop!", "Right-click or use the tray icon anytime to open controls, chat, or hide your companion.", "Interaction Guide"]
8: ["We can notify you on your desktop the moment your pet is ready to play."]
9: ["Adoption Official!", "Your companion certificate is registered. Next, we will load your pet onto your desktop screen.", "Continue to Desktop"]
